speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for sharing your history. To better understand your knee pain, can you describe the specific location of the pain and whether it occurs with any particular movements?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old female. The patient presents with knee pain that started yesterday and has been steadily worsening. She cites recent participation in volleyball involving repetitive pivoting and twisting movements as a possible cause. She was advised at her last physical exam that weight loss could be beneficial for her health.

speaker: Doctor
text: Can you point to the exact spot of the pain and tell me if there is swelling, redness, or warmth around the knee? Also, have you experienced any popping sound or instability when the pain began?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Knee pain, specifically over the medial aspect of the tibia just inferior to the patella. I also have Recent weight loss attempt, Increased physical activity.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Medial tibial stress syndrome (shin splints). REQUEST IMAGES: X-ray of the left tibia to rule out stress fracture.
